newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine arrest orders overruled in IBM case.
newsitem.headline: Argentine arrest orders overruled in IBM case.

text.p: An Argentine appeals court has overruled a judge that ordered the arrest of former executives of state-run Banco Nacion and IBM's local unit on bribery charges.

The upper court ruled the investigator, Judge Adolfo Bagnasco, violated the rights of the suspects by seeking to try them twice for the same crime. He was investigating the executives on allegations of embezzlement and bribery, the latter of which the court said fell under the crime of embezzlement.
Bagnasco can continue to investigate them for embezzlement despite the ruling overturning the arrest orders, the appeals court said.

"This court has read in astonishment the (lower court) ruling that pays no heed of elementary constitutional guarantees," the upper court said in its judgment. "The court hence nullifies...the arrests ordered."

Bagnasco is investigating whether bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure International Business Machines Corp's Argentine unit was awarded a $250 million contract to install a computer system at Banco Nacion.

In May, Bagnasco issued warrants for the arrest of former Banco Nacion head Aldo Dadone, former board member Alfredo Aldaco, a former government official and former IBM Argentina head Ricardo Martorana and his deputy Gustavo Soriani on bribery charges.
Dadone and Aldaco were also accused of embezzling public funds. Five others were indicted in connection with the case.
Aldaco is in jail while Martorana has been set free on bail.
Bagnasco can only investigate the suspects for embezzling, a crime that encompasses bribery, the upper court said.

At the heart of the probe are payments made to IBM's subcontractor CCR, which according to Bagnasco "benefited from a $37 million deal" he suspects went to alleged bribes. The judges believes CCR was used to funnel the alleged illegal payments.
IBM Argentina has denied any wrongdoing, although it has admitted to errors "inconsistent with company policy."

Banco Nacion last year canceled the deal and sued IBM Argentina for $174 million, accusing the company in a Buenos Aires Administrative Contentious Court, which arbitrates commercial disputes, of not complying with deadlines.
IBM countersued for $86 million, alleging "wrongful revocation" of the contract.
Other IBM Argentina deals are the subject of separate probes.
